issues.location: composition lemma representing-term index and conclusion
issues.finding: The given functions end at g_{k-1}, while their representing terms end at G_k; the conclusion says H is lambda definable although h is the function and H is its representing term.
issues.proposed_resolution: Index the final representing term as G_{k-1} and state that h is lambda definable; retain H as its displayed term.

issues.finding: The recurrence uses h, rather than the stipulated (n+2)-ary function g, on its right-hand side and consequently gives h one extra argument. The following prose also names h instead of g as the state-update function.
issues.proposed_resolution: Use g(x_1,...,x_n,y,h(x_1,...,x_n,y)) as the recursive step and describe iteration of the update derived from g.

issues.location: induction display and final lambda abstraction
issues.finding: A row break and alignment tab interrupt the tuple argument in the inductive calculation. Two final-display abstractions write the optional-argument macro as \lambd[p].\tuple rather than supplying its body in the second optional argument.
issues.proposed_resolution: Keep the inductive tuple within one aligned row and write both abstractions as \lambd[p][\tuple{...}].

issues.location: scope of the D abbreviation in H
issues.finding: The displayed update term D contains x free even though H binds x; the abbreviation must be expanded in H's body for that binder to bind the intended occurrence.
issues.proposed_resolution: Explain in the translated prose that D is a schematic abbreviation expanded under H's x binder, as the final displayed expansion already shows.
